policy.causal_rule: A successful code test does not prove a GitHub event trigger was honored. Treat zero-job event metadata as an unresolved operational anomaly until evaluated workflow and event-delivery evidence exist.

nodes.label: Push event run with zero jobs on PR #1344 branch

edges.claim: PR #1344 adds safety/** and fix/** push triggers with a read-only no-op job and scopes pull-requests:write to workflow_dispatch. Exact-head CI and gate passed; PR remains draft/unmerged.
The branch's own push run still reports failure and zero jobs despite the branch-specific trigger/no-op definition. The event/run mismatch remains unresolved.

competing_hypotheses.claim: GitHub may be evaluating the default-branch workflow definition for the observed push run, so branch-only trigger changes would not govern it until merged.
disconfirming_evidence: No workflow evaluation trace or job log is available; the run metadata alone does not prove which workflow version was evaluated.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The push event with zero jobs may reflect a GitHub Actions event-delivery or run-metadata anomaly.
disconfirming_evidence: No independent GitHub incident record or event delivery log was found.
